body.statement: For fixed \((\eta,G,B,C,\alpha)\), iid draws \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\sim P\), and \(\mathcal C_n\) from \(\mathrm{def{:}multiplier\text{-}confidence\text{-}set}\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_\eta}P\{[F_-(P),F_+(P)]\subseteq\mathcal C_n\}\geq1-\alpha\). On the nonfallback event, \(w_n=O_P(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_\eta\). The result permits active branch ties, redundant branches, singular covariance matrices, and branch-gradient coordinates with zero variance.
body.justification: Applications require sampling uncertainty for the entire identified interval, not pointwise standard errors for a selected smooth branch.
body.gap: Tan (2025) leaves sample inference open; Bonvini et al. (2022) and Zhang and Zhao (2026) use different sensitivity models, while Fang and Santos (2019) does not itself yield this all-branch uniform causal-interval guarantee.
body.consumer: It gives a uniformly honest confidence set for the absolute sustained-metformin cancer-risk interval in a discretized target-trial analysis.
